title: Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting
wiki_lead:
On December 14, 2012, a mass shooting occurred at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut, in which 20-year-old Adam Lanza killed 26 people—20 first-grade children and six staff members—before killing himself. Lanza had earlier fatally shot his mother at their home before driving to the school, where he forced entry by shooting out a window near the locked front entrance. He was armed with a semi-automatic rifle and two handguns and killed the victims within about five minutes, before shooting himself as police arrived. It is the deadliest mass shooting at a K–12 school in U.S. history and the fourth-deadliest mass shooting by a single perpetrator in the nation.
A November 2013 report issued by the Connecticut State Attorney's office stated that Lanza acted alone and planned his actions, but provided no indication of why he did so, or why he targeted the school. A report issued by the Office of the Child Advocate in November 2014 released that Lanza had Asperger's syndrome and, as a teenager, suffered from depression, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and anorexia, but concluded that these factors "neither caused nor led to his murderous acts". The report went on to say, "his severe and deteriorating internalized mental health problems [...] combined with an atypical preoccupation with violence [...] (and) access to deadly weapons [...] proved a recipe for mass murder."
The shooting renewed national debate over gun control, mental health policy, and school safety. President Barack Obama visited Newtown days later and formed a federal task force on gun violence; his administration subsequently announced a series of executive actions in January 2013. Proposed federal legislation to expand background checks and restrict certain semi-automatic weapons failed in the Senate that April, though Connecticut and dozens of other states went on to pass their own gun-control measures.
Victims' families founded several gun-violence-prevention organizations after the shooting, including Sandy Hook Promise and Moms Demand Action. The attack also became the subject of persistent hoax conspiracy theories, promoted most prominently by media personality Alex Jones, who was later ordered to pay victims' families nearly $1.5 billion in defamation damages. The original school building was demolished and replaced with a new one on the same site in 2016, and a permanent memorial to the 26 victims was dedicated in 2022.

Background
Sandy Hook Elementary School, which served students in kindergarten through fourth grade, was located at 12 Dickinson Drive within the Newtown Public Schools district. It was built in 1956 to relieve overcrowding in the town’s schools amid rapid population growth; Newtown’s population rose from 4,023 in 1940 to 7,448 in 1950. The building was designed by New York City architect Louis E. Jallade, whom the town chose for his specialization in school design, and stood on a 12-acre site the town had purchased from John Stefanko.
grok_lead: On December 14, 2012, 20-year-old Adam Lanza carried out a mass killing at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Newtown, Connecticut. There, he shot and killed 20 first-grade children aged 6 and 7, plus 6 adult staff members, using a Bushmaster XM15-E2S rifle. Before attacking the school, Lanza killed his mother, Nancy Lanza, at home by shooting her four times in the head with a.22-caliber rifle. The school events lasted under eight minutes. Lanza then died by suicide from a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head. Connecticut authorities investigated and concluded Lanza acted alone. Forensic analysis, survivor eyewitness accounts, and physical evidence such as shell casings and victim autopsies showed no accomplices or outside involvement. Lanza showed deep social isolation, untreated mental health issues including obsessive-compulsive disorder and possible undiagnosed conditions, and an obsession with mass shootings. Behavioral analyses and his personal writings revealed this after the event. He had left formal education, rarely went outside, and gathered detailed information on past mass killings. He obsessively edited online entries about them. Lanza gained access to firearms through his mother's legal collection. It included the AR-15 variant, which she had bought and kept at home despite his instability. Lanza had no prior criminal record or direct warnings about the attack. Yet family and medical records noted missed chances to intervene as his condition worsened. This event was the deadliest K-12 school shooting in U.S. history by number of child victims. It revealed weaknesses in mental health monitoring, school security, and agency information sharing, as state reviews found. The shooting led to efforts for better background checks, limits on assault weapons, and threat assessment systems. Federal changes were small, but Connecticut added rules like required reporting of mental health risks and stronger school defenses. Claims of a staged event or crisis actors spread by some despite evidence like ballistic reports and survivor statements. These have led to defamation suits and more focus on online misinformation.
